title: Chapter 1: UNDERSTANDING DISABILITIES AND VULNERABILITIES
content:
ሰላም ሰላም በጣም የምንወዳችሁ እና የምናከብራችሁ የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦቻችን! 👋 🎁 ከቤተሰባዊ ፍቅርና አክብሮት ጋር እንኳን ወደ Inclusiveness Chapter 1 Part 1 ትምህርት በሰላም መጣችሁ! እኛ የEthioFresh ቲሞች የዩኒቨርሲቲ ቆይታችሁ አልጋ በአልጋ እንዲሆንላችሁ እና በፈተና ወቅት ያለምንም ስጋት A+ እንድታስመዘግቡ በበቂ ሁኔታ የሚያዘጋጃችሁን ኖት ይዘንላችሁ መጥተናል። 📌 በዚህ የመጀመሪያው ክፍል ቆይታችን የምንዳስሳቸው ዋና ዋና ርዕሶች : * 1.1 Basic Terms: Impairment, Disability, and Handicap * Models of Disability: Medical Model vs. Social Model * 1.2 Causes of Disability: Historical misconceptions and scientific causes (Genetic, Environmental, Unknown, Inaccessible environments) * 1.3 Types of Disabilities (Part 1): 1. Visual Impairment (Blindness & Low Vision) 2. Hearing Impairment (Hard of Hearing & Deaf) 3. Specific Learning Disability - SLD (Subtypes: APD, Dyscalculia, Dysgraphia, Dyslexia, LPD, NVLD, Visual Perceptual Deficit) 4. Speech and Language Impairments (Articulation, Fluency, Voice, Phonological, Morphological, Semantic, Syntactic, Pragmatics) 5. Autism (Key characteristics, Language features, Pronoun reversal, Echolalia) 6. Emotional and Behavioral Disorders - EBD (IDEA criteria, Classifications, Kauffman classifications, Causes) አንድም ሀሳብ ሳናስቀር እንመርምረው! 🚀✨ --- 1.1 BASIC TERMS (IMPAIRMENT, DISABILITY AND HANDICAP) 1. Impairment * Impairment means a lack/abnormality of an anatomic, physiological, or psychological structure or function or deviation on a person. It refers to any loss or abnormality of physiological, psychological, or anatomical structure or function. It is the absence of a particular body part or organ, or a condition in which the body exists but doesn't function typically. * Examples: - Eyes that do not see well - Arms and legs that are deformed - Brain not developing in a typical way 2. Disability * The term disability is ambiguous as there is no single agreement on the concept (Mitra, 2006). The concept of disability is complex, dynamic, multidimensional, and contested (WHO and World Bank, 2011). * Crucial Terminology Distinction: Disability is NOT synonymous with AKAL-GUDATENGA (የአካል ጉዳተኛ). In the Ethiopian context, AKAL-GUDATENGA (የአካል ጉዳተኛ) actually refers to impairment. * Disabling Factors (Barriers to Full Inclusion): 1. Attitudinal Barriers: Societal barriers, such as stigma, prejudice, and discrimination. 2. Physical Barriers: Environmental barriers, meaning the absence of stairs/ramps and inaccessible infrastructure. 3. Policy Barriers: Systemic barriers in laws, institutional rules, and policies. * Core Principle: Societal, environmental, and systemic barriers are the most popular disabling factors. If these problems are addressed, an impairment may NOT lead to a disability! * Preferred Terminology: Always use "Persons with disability" rather than "A disabled person". 👉 Impairment (የአካል/የአእምሮ ጉዳት) ማለት የሰውነት አካል ወይም የአእምሮ መዋቅር ባዮሎጂካል መጎደል ወይም አለመስራት ነው። ለምሳሌ የአይን አለማየት፣ የእግር መቆረጥ ወይም የአእምሮ አለመልማት ናቸው። በኢትዮጵያ ነባራዊ ሁኔታ "የአካል ጉዳተኛ" የምንለው ቃል የሚያመለክተው Impairmentን እንጂ Disabilityን አይደለም! Disability (የተሳትፎ ውሱንነት) የሚፈጠረው ደግሞ ማህበረሰቡ በሚፈጥራቸው 3 መሰናክሎች (Attitudinal-አመለካከት/ማግለል፣ Physical-መንገድና ህንፃ፣ Policy-ህግና መመሪያ) ምክንያት Impairment ያለው ሰው ከሌላው ጋር እኩል እንዳይሳተፍ ሲከለከል ነው። እነዚህን መሰናክሎች ካስወገድን Impairment ያለበት ሰው Disability አይኖረውም!
💡 Exam Hint: Onetime exam question alert! Teachers love asking: "Does impairment always lead to disability?" The answer is NO! Impairment only turns into a disability when society creates attitudinal, physical, or policy barriers!
--- MODELS OF DISABILITY 1. Medical Approach (Medical Model) * Views disability as a pathology (physiological, biological, and intellectual). Disability means functional limitations due to physical, intellectual, or psychic impairment, health, or psychic disorders on a person (WHO, 1996). * Core Premise: Disabled persons are individual objects to be "treated", "changed", or "improved" to be made more "normal". * It demands that the individual "fits in" to society rather than society changing. It fails to account for interaction between societal conditions and individual circumstances. 2. Social Model * Views disability as a complex condition with a range of implications for social identity and behavior. * Disability depends on context and is a consequence of discrimination, prejudice, and exclusion. * Emphasizes the shortcomings of the environment and organized social activities (information, communication, education).
📊 Comparison: Medical Model vs. Social Model
* 🔴 Medical Model: Child is faulty | 🟢 Social Model: Child is valued * 🔴 Medical Model: Diagnosis and labeling | 🟢 Social Model: Strengths and needs identified * 🔴 Medical Model: Impairment is focus of attention | 🟢 Social Model: Barriers identified and solutions developed * 🔴 Medical Model: Segregation and alternative services | 🟢 Social Model: Resources made available * 🔴 Medical Model: Re-entry if normal enough or permanent exclusion | 🟢 Social Model: Diversity welcomed; child is welcomed * 🔴 Medical Model: Society remains unchanged | 🟢 Social Model: Society evolves
👉 Medical Model ችግሩ በሙሉ ያለው ግለሰቡ አካል/አእምሮ ላይ ነው ብሎ ያስባል (Pathology)። ግለሰቡ መታከም፣ መቀየር ወይም መጠገን አለበት ይላል እንጂ ማህበረሰቡና አካባቢው እንዲቀየሩ አይጠይቅም። Social Model ደግሞ በበኩሉ ችግሩ ያለው ግለሰቡ ላይ ሳይሆን ማህበረሰቡ በሚፈጥረው አድሎ፣ ማግለል እና ተስማሚ ያልሆነ አካባቢ ነው ይላል። ስለዚህ ግለሰቡን ሳይሆን ማህበረሰቡንና አካባቢውን መለወጥ አለብን ብሎ ያምናል። 😅 EthioFresh Humor Break: የቲም አባላቶቻችንን "ትምህርት አልገባኝም" ስትሏቸው "ችግሩ የአንተ አእምሮ ነው" ካሏችሁ Medical Model ተጠቀሙ ማለት ነው! "አስተማማኝ ማስታወሻ ስላልሰጠናችሁ ነው" ካላችኋቸው ግን Social Model ገብቷችኋል ማለት ነው! 😂
💡 Exam Hint: Be ready for matching or true/false questions on these models! Remember: Medical Model = Fix the Individual; Social Model = Fix the Environment & Society!
--- 1.2 CAUSES OF DISABILITY Historical Misconceptions: * In the past, people wrongly believed that disability is a punishment from God or karma for past mistakes. The module stresses that this is totally unacceptable today! Scientific Causes: 1. Genetic Causes * Abnormalities in genes and genetic inheritance can cause intellectual disability in children. * Examples: Down syndrome is the most common genetic condition. Over-exposure to X-rays, diseases, and illnesses can also cause genetic disorders. 2. Environmental Factors * Poverty & Malnutrition: Malnutrition in pregnant mothers causes mineral deficiencies leading to deformation in unborn children. Post-birth malnutrition causes poor development of vital organs. * Substance & Chemical Exposure: Use of drugs, alcohol, tobacco, and exposure to toxic chemicals during pregnancy. * Maternal Infections: Toxoplasmosis, Cytomegalovirus, Rubella, and Syphilis in a pregnant mother. * Childhood Diseases: Whooping cough, measles, and chicken pox leading to meningitis and encephalitis (causing brain damage). * Toxic Materials: Lead and mercury damaging the brain. * Unfortunate Life Events: Drowning, automobile accidents, falls leading to loss of sight, hearing, or limbs. 3. Unknown Causes * Unexplained cellular, brain, and gene development anomalies that scientists have not yet fully understood. 4. Inaccessible Environments * Infrastructure built without ramps (only stairs) making movement impossible. Lack of education, support services, and opportunities turns impairments into severe disabilities. 👉 የጉዳት መንስኤዎችን በጥንት ጊዜ ሰዎች የእግዚአብሔር/የአላህ ቁጣ ወይም የኃጢአት ውጤት አድርገው ያስቡ ነበር፤ ይህም ፍፁም ስህተት ነው። ሳይንሳዊ መንስኤዎቹ፦ Genetic (የጂንና የዘር ውርስ ችግር ለምሳሌ Down syndrome)፣ Environmental (የእናትና የሕፃን የምግብ እጥረት፣ አረቄ/ሲጋራ/እጽ፣ እናቶች ላይ የሚከሰቱ Toxoplasmosis/Rubella ኢንፌክሽኖች፣ የልጅነት ኩፍኝ፣ ሊድና ሜርኩሪ፣ የመኪናና የመስጠም አደጋዎች)፣ Unknown Causes (በሳይንስ ያልታወቁ የሴልና አእምሮ እክሎች) እና Inaccessible Environments (ተስማሚ ያልሆኑ ህንፃዎችና መንገዶች) ናቸው።
💡 Exam Hint: Multi-choice questions frequently list causes. Make sure you remember that Maternal Infections (Toxoplasmosis, Rubella, Syphilis) and Toxic materials (Lead, Mercury) belong to Environmental causes!
--- 1.3 TYPES OF DISABILITIES 1. Visual Impairment * Blindness: Total or partial inability to see due to disease or disorder of the eye, optic nerve, or brain. Not correctable by eyeglasses or contact lenses. (Note: Some blind individuals may still perceive slowly moving lights or colors). * Low Vision: Moderately impaired vision affecting central vision (directly in front) or peripheral vision (sides/behind). They still process information primarily through vision using adaptations. 👉 Visual Impairment በሁለት ይከፈላል፦ Blindness (በመነፅር ሊስተካከል የማይችል ሙሉ ወይም በከፊል የማየት ችግር) እና Low vision (መካከለኛ የማየት ችግር ሆኖ visual informationን በዋናነት የሚጠቀሙ) ናቸው። 2. Hearing Impairment * A generic term indicating a continuum of hearing loss from mild to profound (Pasonella and Carat). * Hard of Hearing: Hearing impairment (permanent or fluctuating) that adversely affects educational performance but is not included under 'deaf' (Whelan, 1988). Uses hearing aids as a primary modality of language acquisition. * Deaf: Difficulty understanding speech even with hearing aids. Communicates successfully using sign language and connects with the culturally deaf community. 👉 Hearing Impairment በሁለት ይከፈላል፦ Hard of Hearing (በመስማያ መሳሪያ በመታገዝ ድምፅ መስማትና መማር የሚችሉ) እና Deaf (በመስማያ መሳሪያ እንኳን ድምፅ መለየት የማይችሉና በምልክት ቋንቋ የሚግባቡ) ናቸው። 3. Specific Learning Disability (SLD) * A disorder in one or more of the basic psychological processes involved in understanding or using language (spoken or written), manifesting in imperfect ability to listen, think, speak, read, write, spell, or do math calculations. * Includes: Perceptual disabilities, brain injury, minimal brain dysfunction, dyslexia, developmental aphasia. * Excludes: Learning problems resulting primarily from visual, hearing, or motor disabilities, intellectual disability, emotional disturbance, or environmental/economic disadvantage. * Golden Trait: Generally, people with learning disabilities have AVERAGE or ABOVE AVERAGE intelligence! They are referred to as having "hidden disabilities" due to the gap between potential and actual achievement. It is a lifelong challenge. Subtypes of Specific Learning Disability (SLD): * Auditory Processing Disorder (APD): (Central APD) Affects how sound is processed/interpreted by the brain. Difficulty recognizing subtle sound differences, locating sound sources, or blocking background noise. * A. Dyscalculia: Specific LD affecting ability to understand numbers and math. Poor comprehension of math symbols, difficulty memorizing/organizing numbers, telling time, and counting. * B. Dysgraphia: Specific LD affecting handwriting ability and fine motor skills. Causes illegible handwriting, inconsistent spacing, poor spatial planning, poor spelling, and difficulty writing while thinking. * C. Dyslexia: Specific LD affecting reading and related language-based processing skills. Affects reading fluency, decoding, reading comprehension, recall, writing, and spelling. Also called Language-Based Learning Disability. * D. Language Processing Disorder (LPD): Specific APD with difficulty attaching meaning to sound groups, words, and sentences. Relates specifically to language processing (expressive/receptive). * E. Non-Verbal Learning Disabilities (NVLD / NLD): Discrepancy between higher verbal skills and weaker motor, visual-spatial, and social skills. Trouble interpreting nonverbal cues (facial expressions, body language) and poor coordination. * F. Visual Perceptual/Visual Motor Deficit: Affects understanding of visual information, drawing/copying. Causes missing subtle shape/letter differences, losing place frequently, struggles with cutting, holding pencil too tightly, or poor eye/hand coordination. 👉 Specific Learning Disability (SLD) ያለባቸው ተማሪዎች መካከለኛ ወይምዚያ በላይ የሆነ አእምሮአዊ ብቃት (Average or Above Average IQ) አላቸው! አእምሮአቸው በጣም ንቁ ሆኖ ሳለ የትምህርት ውጤታቸው ዝቅተኛ ስለሚሆን "Hidden Disability" ይባላሉ። ዓይነቶቹ፦ Dyscalculia (የቁጥርና የሂሳብ ችግር)፣ Dysgraphia (የእጅ ጽሁፍና የጣት Fine Motor skills ችግር)፣ Dyslexia (የንባብ፣ ፊደል የመለየትና የቃላት መፍታት ችግር)፣ APD/LPD (ድምፅንና ቋንቋን በአእምሮ የመተርጎም እክል)፣ NVLD (የሰዎችን የፊት ገጽታና የሰውነት እንቅስቃሴ አለመረዳት) እና Visual Perceptual Deficit (የምስሎችንና የፊደላትን ቅርጽ የመለየት ችግር) ናቸው። 😅 EthioFresh Humor Break: Exam ላይ 1+1=3 ካላችሁ Dyscalculia የለባችሁም፤ ጥናት ማነስ ነው! አትሸወዱ! 😂
💡 Exam Hint: Matching questions on SLD subtypes are 100% guaranteed in final exams! Memorize: Dyscalculia = Math, Dysgraphia = Handwriting/Fine Motor, Dyslexia = Reading, NVLD = Body Language/Facial Cues!
4. Speech and Language Impairments Speech Impairments: * Articulation Disorders: Errors in producing speech sounds due to anatomical, muscular, or neuromuscular limitations: - Omissions: Example: "bo for boat" - Substitutions: Example: "wabbit for rabbit" - Distortions: Example: "shlip for sip" * Fluency Disorders: Difficulties with speech rhythm and timing: - Stuttering: Rapid-fire repetitions of consonant/vowel sounds, prolongations, hesitations, verbal blocks. - Cluttering: Excessively fast and jerky speech. * Voice Disorders: Problems with quality, pitch, loudness, resonance, or duration due to larynx disorders. Language Impairments: * Phonological Disorders: Abnormal organization of the phonological system. Includes Apraxia of speech (difficulty planning speech motor movements). * Morphological Disorders: Difficulties with morphological inflections on nouns, verbs, and adjectives. * Semantic Disorders: Poor vocabulary development, inappropriate word meanings, excessive use of nonspecific terms (Example: "thing and stuff"), and indefinite references (Example: "that and there"). * Syntactic Deficits: Difficulty with grammar rules and word order (subject-verb agreement). Produces shorter, less elaborate sentences with fewer conjunctions. * Pragmatic Difficulties: Problems using language in social contexts (poor eye contact, failing to respect personal space, requesting info, introducing topics). 👉 Speech Impairments የድምፅ አወጣጥ ችግሮች ሲሆኑ (Articulation: Omission - ፊደል ማስቀረት "bo for boat"፣ Substitution - ፊደል መቀየር "wabbit for rabbit"፣ Distortion - ድምፅ ማበላሸት፤ Fluency: Stuttering - መንተባተብ፣ Cluttering - በፍጥነት መናገር) ናቸው። Language Impairments ደግሞ የቋንቋ ህግጋትን የመረዳት ችግር ሲሆን (Semantics: "thing and stuff" የሚሉ አጠቃላይ ቃላትን ማበዛት፤ Syntactic: የሰዋሰው ስህተት፤ Pragmatics: የማህበራዊ ግንኙነትና የአይን ግንኙነት ህግጋትን አለመረዳት) ናቸው።
💡 Exam Hint: Exam questions directly copy examples like "bo for boat" (Omission) and "thing and stuff" (Semantic Disorder). Master these exact phrases!
5. Autism * Developmental disability affecting verbal/nonverbal communication and social interaction, evident before age three, adversely affecting educational performance. * Characteristics: Repetitive activities, stereotyped movements, resistance to routine changes, unusual sensory responses. * Language & Speech Features in Autism: - Personal pronoun reversal: Example: using "I" instead of "you" and vice-versa. - Misuse of prepositions: Example: misusing "in", "on", "under", "next to". - Echolalia: Formal repetition of other people's utterances (Arron and Gittens, 1999). 👉 Autism ከ3 ዓመት እድሜ በፊት የሚገለፅ የአእምሮ እድገት ውሱንነት ሲሆን፤ ተደጋገሚ እንቅስቃሴዎች፣ የቋንቋ ችግር (Pronoun Reversal - "እኔ" እና "አንተ" ማቀያየር፣ Prepositions ማበላሸት) እና Echolalia (የሰሙትን ቃል ወይም ዓረፍተ ነገር መልሶ በተደጋጋሚ ማለት) ይታይባቸዋል።
💡 Exam Hint: Always remember the age threshold for Autism diagnosis onset (before age 3) and the 3 specific language impairments (Pronoun reversal, Preposition misuse, Echolalia)!
6. Emotional and Behavioral Disorders (EBD) * IDEA Criteria: Condition exhibiting one or more characteristics over a long period and to a marked degree adversely affecting educational performance: 1. Inability to learn not explained by intellectual, sensory, or health factors. 2. Inability to build/maintain satisfactory interpersonal relationships with peers and teachers. 3. Inappropriate types of behavior or feelings under normal circumstances. 4. General pervasive mood of unhappiness or depression. 5. Tendency to develop physical symptoms or fears associated with personal or school problems. Classifications of Behavioral and Emotional Disorders: * Conduct Disorder: Overt (violence, tantrums) vs. Covert (lying, stealing, drug use). * Socialized Aggression: Joining subcultures of peers disrespectful to peers/teachers/parents. Delinquency and dropping out. Early symptoms: stealing, running away, habitual lying, cruelty to animals, fire setting. * Attention Problems: Attention deficit, easily distractible, poor concentration, impulsive. * Anxiety / Withdrawn: Self-conscious, reserved, low self-esteem, withdraws, anxious, depressed. * Psychotic Behavior: Bizarre behavior, hallucinations, fantasy world, talking in gibberish. * Motor Excess: Hyperactive, cannot sit or listen. Kauffman (1993) Classifications: 1. Externalizing Behavior (Under-controlled): Disobedience, disruptiveness, fighting, temper tantrums, irresponsibility, anger, attention seeking. 2. Internalizing Behavior (Over-controlled): Anxiety, immaturity, shyness, social withdrawal, feeling of inadequacy (inferiority), guilt, depression, excessive worrying. Causes of Behavioral and Emotional Disorders: 1. Biological: Genetic disorders, brain damage, malnutrition, allergies, temperament, CNS damage. 2. Family Factors: Family interactions, child abuse, neglect, poor home discipline. 3. Cultural Factors: Negative cultural practices (watching violence/sexually oriented media). 4. Environmental Factors: Peer pressure, poverty, unresponsive schooling practices. 👉 EBD በትምህርት አፈፃፀም ላይ አሉታዊ ተፅዕኖ የሚያሳድር የባህሪና የስሜት እክል ነው። Kauffman በሁለት ዋና ዋና ክፍሎች ይከፍለዋል፦ Externalizing (Under-controlled) - ወደ ውጭ የሚወጡ ቁጣ፣ ረብሻ፣ ፀብና እምቢተኝነት ሲሆኑ፤ Internalizing (Over-controlled) - ደግሞ ወደ ውስጥ የሚታመቁ ጭንቀት፣ ፍርሃት፣ ድብርትና ከሰው መገለል ናቸው። መንስኤዎቹም ባዮሎጂካል፣ የቤተሰብ አያያዝ፣ ባህላዊ እና የአካባቢ ሁኔታዎች ናቸው።
💡 Exam Hint: Kauffman's classifications (Externalizing vs Internalizing) are super hot exam targets! Remember: Externalizing = Under-controlled (acting out/fighting), Internalizing = Over-controlled (anxiety/shyness/depression)!
